newsitem.title: USA: Dupont reports record second-quarter earnings.
newsitem.headline: Dupont reports record second-quarter earnings.

text.p: Chemical giant DuPont Co. on Wednesday reported record second-quarter profits, a 14 percent jump fuelled by strong performances from the company's fibers and petroleum businesses.

Net income hit $1.14 billion, or $1.01 per share, in the quarter ended June 30, compared with $1 billion, or 89 cents a share, in last year's second quarter. Per-share results reflected a 2-for-1 stock split that took effect May 15.
The earnings by one of the nation's biggest chemical companies were in line with analysts' expectations, according to market research firm First Call.
Sales totalled $11.4 billion for the quarter, a 2 percent increase from $11.1 billion a year ago.

A strong dollar held back revenues in the core chemicals and specialities unit by reducing prices relative to the dollar of DuPont products overseas, the company said. Excluding the effects of currencies, selling prices were 1 percent lower.
But officials said they were encouraged by volume gains of 10 percent in the division.
DuPont's stock rose $1.56 to $67.625 on the New York Stock Exchange.

The Wilmington, Del.-based company, known for developing products like nylon and spandex, said the quarter's results reflected record earnings by its fibers and polymers units, combined with continued strong performance by its Conoco petroleum unit, particularly in refining and marketing.
DuPont's second-quarter fiber-segment earnings rose 18 percent from a year earlier, to $245 million.

"Our speciality fiber products, especially Lycra, are doing extraordinarly well on a global basis, to the point that we will probably be expanding capacity significantly to meet worldwide demand," Chief Financial Officer Kurt Landgraf told a telephone news conference.
Landgraf said DuPont's board had not yet approved the expansion plans and he could not comment in detail. "We will be announcing these things in the relative near future," he said.

The Dacron business has in the last year experienced a "very important" turnaround in earnings after four or five years of losses, Landgraf said. This was achieved by improved market share and cost cuts, he said.
DuPont said its agricultural products business also had a strong quarter and was a key contributor to growth in chemicals and specialities.
For the first half of 1997, DuPont earned $2.2 billion, or $1.91 a share, compared with $1.9 billion, or $1.68 a share, last year.

"We are well on our way to a fourth consecutive year of record earnings," DuPont President John Krol said in a statement. "Total return to DuPont shareholders was 36 percent for the first half of this year, exceeding industry averages."
DuPont's petroleum business earned $246 million, a second-quarter record and up 13 percent from $218 million last year. Polymers made $259 million, up 6 percent from $244 million in 1996.
Earnings from chemicals slipped 17 percent to $137 million from $165 million in the year-ago period.
